race: Formula 1 Gran Premio de la Ciudad de México 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to Mexico City, where a Ferrari pole position has turned the whole weekend upside down and made everyone sit up.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Lewis Hamilton took his first pole for Ferrari, and his first in more than three years, with the crowd loving every second.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: And what a timing, with Kimi Antonelli chasing history right behind the wheel, and the title fight suddenly feeling alive.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The story is tense, but Hamilton stole the day and handed Red Bull a headache, while the young champion had to wait his turn.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Max Verstappen gets a one place grid penalty from the practice collision, so the start gets spicy, and the midfield gets nervous.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Now the real question, can Ferrari convert that pole into a win, or does the penalty turn it into a long, tricky recovery?

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: I say yes, because Hamilton's Mexico record is warm, with an average of fourth point seven, and the car feels ready to deliver.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: His best is second, and he has one podium over three races, so the wall is there, but he has also learned how to attack it.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: But the penalty is huge, a fifty place grid penalty for power unit elements, which means he starts from nowhere in the field.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: So he starts from the back of the pack, and that is a whole different race, full of traffic, risk, and every kind of opportunity.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is why Charles Leclerc is my second pick, because he is the Ferrari safety net, and he has the speed to lead from the front.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Leclerc was fastest in practice, and his Mexico history is scary, which is exactly why I would not bet against him on Sunday.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Average second point seven, best second, and three podiums over three races, so this track feels like home ground for him.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is not luck, that is a driver who has won the rhythm of this track, and he knows how to make a strong car feel stronger.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: So why is George Russell third? I know the grid is stacked, but Mercedes have been fast enough to keep everyone honest.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Because Mercedes qualified second, and their pace is still very real, so a clean run could put them right in the mix.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: His Mexico history is colder, average sixth, best fifth, and no podiums in three races, but that is exactly why the upset is tempting.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: But a clean race from second could put him ahead of both Ferraris, and a good tyre strategy could turn a tricky start into a podium.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is the gamble I love, and it is why he is in our top three, because he can be quiet, patient, and then suddenly very fast.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: My deep cut is Oscar Piastri, starting from twelfth, because McLaren can overtake here, and a small mistake can become a big jump.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: He has recent top six form, and a good start can turn into a top ten finish, even if the grid does not make it easy for him.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is the kind of upset we live for, and it is the kind of story that makes Mexico City feel like a proper race weekend.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: The grid is full of surprises, and this one feels especially juicy, because every car is chasing a different kind of victory.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Ferrari want a one two, Mercedes want to spoil it, and Red Bull want to remind everyone they know how to win at this track.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Here is the full top ten, Hamilton, Leclerc, Russell, Verstappen, Antonelli, Norris, Hadjar, Lindblad, Gasly, and Piastri.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: So keep an eye on the first corner, because the penalty, the pace, and the pressure could all collide in one chaotic moment.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: We will be here when the lights go out, and we will be here when the dust settles, because this is the moment formula one lives for.
